item.title: Setback for C’River NDC as Deputy Governorship candidate quits, backs Otu
item.description: …governorship candidate expresses shock By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Cross River State has suffered a setback ahead of the 2027 governorship election, following the withdrawal of its Deputy Governorship candidate, Mrs. Stella Charles Archibong, from the party’s ticket. Archibong announced her exit in a statement made available to newsmen in Calabar on Wednesday, declaring support for Governor Bassey Otu’s re-election bid under the Back to South Movement. She said her decision followed extensive consultations with elders, family members, the Christian community and political stakeholders across the state. According to her, her responsibility to Cross River was greater than her personal political ambition, hence her resolve to align with the political direction of the Otu administration. “My responsibility to Cross River State is bigger than my individual ambition,” she declared. Archibong also expressed appreciation to the NDC State Chairman, Mr. Goddy Akpama, the party’s governorship candidate, Mr. John Odey, and the national leadership for the opportunity to serve on the party’s platform. She apologised to supporters who might feel disappointed by her decision, and thanked them for their support and confidence throughout her political engagement. Reacting, Odey described her withdrawal as surprising, but urged party members and supporters to remain calm and demonstrate maturity. In a statement, he said the development required calmness, mutual respect and responsible leadership. “This development has come as a surprise. I believe that moments such as this call for calm, maturity, mutual respect, and responsible leadership,” he said. Odey said he held Archibong in high regard and respected her contributions and commitment to the aspirations of Cross River. He disclosed that consultations were ongoing with party leaders, stakeholders and concerned individuals to understand the circumstances surrounding her withdrawal and determine the appropriate next steps. The NDC candidate, however, assured supporters that the party remained committed to building a prosperous, inclusive and economically productive state. item.title: Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Late President Muhammadu Buhari’s instinct, when the Niger Delta Avengers began to press the state through sabotage and threat, was to bring “the weight of the armed forces against the insurgents”, an excerpt from his authorised biography has revealed. The account, credited to former Minister of State, Petroleum, Dr Ibe Kachikwu, is contained in “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume work to be publicly presented on Thursday, 19 November 2026, at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. Chairman of the Planning Committee and former Minister of Water Resources, Engr. Suleiman Adamu announced the presentation at a press conference on Wednesday in Abuja. According to an excerpt od the biography read at the event, “Buhari’s instinct, Kachikwu recalled, was command.” It states: “He felt as a general, he should watch Nigeria, he owed her, and he wanted to act militarily. But Kachikwu argued that a purely military response would create complications. The federal forces were already stretched, escalation could paralyze the entire industry.” The disagreement reached a head ahead of a meeting with the Pan-Niger Delta Forum. “The president was present, and Kachikwu was present,” the book records. “Buhari was upset at what was unfolding in Niger Delta and was very reluctant to approve dialogue with militants.” The excerpt says that, after persuasion, Buhari accepted engagement, “allowing the peace process to proceed.” The excerpt notes that Buhari “was unwilling to tolerate what he regarded as ransom politics, but was nudged into engagement.” It adds that one of Kachikwu’s favourite photographs of the late President was taken just after that meeting, “when he finally smiled because he had been tense.” Kachikwu teased him afterwards. “See, it’s not so bad after all,” Buhari smiled, he said. The author, Dr Udu Yakubu noted that the late President cooperated with the project but did not control its content. “The work was authorised by President Buhari. That authorisation opened doors,” he said, adding: “The subject has had his voice in the biography, while the biographer has had or retained his independence.” The post Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate summons NCC, MTN, others over dropped calls, airtime deductions
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, and telecommunications operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent dropped calls, failed connections and unexplained airtime deductions suffered by subscribers. The NCC and telecommunication operators are expected to appear before Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, Zamfara Central-led Senate Committee on Communications. The Committee was mandated to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission and telecommunications operators to investigate complaints of airtime deductions for failed calls, dropped calls, prematurely terminated conversations and inflated charges. The committee is also expected to establish the financial losses suffered by subscribers and report back to the Senate within four weeks, with recommendations for further legislative and regulatory action. The resolution of the Senate on Wednesday was a sequel to a motion titled “Need to curb unjustified deductions from subscribers’ airtime resulting from substandard telecommunications services through robust consumer protection.” The motion was sponsored by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, who seconded the motion, described the proposal as a straightforward consumer-protection intervention, insisting that the problem affects virtually every Nigerian who relies on telecommunications services. He lamented the contrast between the quality of telephone services in Nigeria and the seamless connectivity experienced in other countries. Presenting the motion on behalf of Monguno, the Deputy Majority Leader, Senator Lola Ashiru, APC, Kwara South, expressed concerns over consumers being charged for calls that were never successfully completed, with lawmakers demanding accountability, refunds and improved quality of service across the telecommunications industry. According to the Senate, for millions of Nigerians, making a telephone call has increasingly become an expensive gamble, just as poor network connectivity, dropped calls, interrupted conversations and failed connections have become recurring complaints among subscribers, many of whom lose airtime even when calls are not successfully completed. Senators warned that Nigerians should not be made to pay for telecommunications services that have not been effectively delivered. They noted that subscribers are frequently compelled to redial numbers several times before establishing a connection, resulting in additional airtime deductions and financial losses, particularly for low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners. The Senate argued that while network challenges may sometimes be unavoidable, consumers should not bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for $7.7bn external borrowing plan in 2026 budget
item.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. He further argued that the proceeds would contribute to the country’s external reserves, as the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate. item.title: Otti urges lawyers to defend rights of vulnerable Nigerians
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners across the country to prioritise access to justice by extending legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Otti made the call in Umuahia while declaring open the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference, with the theme, “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development.” The governor urged lawyers to adopt a more humane approach to cases involving indigent and vulnerable citizens, stressing that the pursuit of justice should take precedence over professional interests and financial considerations. He said the legal profession had a responsibility to provide assistance to people who lacked the financial capacity to defend their rights. “And because you are lawyers, we need to go the extra mile of asking ourselves, beyond all the things that have been said, how can we be of service to people who cannot pay? “How can we be of service to the vulnerable? How can we help people who on their own cannot afford to help themselves? “Until government gets to that level, we have not cracked the surface. If it is only about you and then the money you make and all that, then you don’t need to be here. You may as well go and do something else,” he said. Otti said his administration had discovered cases of people who remained in correctional facilities despite allegedly having committed no offences warranting their continued detention. He cited the case of an individual who was allegedly detained for supporting an opposition political party, adding that the experience prompted him to direct the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to work with the Chief Judge to secure the release of such inmates. The governor also warned against the misuse of the justice system to punish citizens for expressing their opinions or engaging in activities on social media, insisting that the protection of individual rights must remain central to governance. On judicial infrastructure, Otti disclosed that his administration would soon commission 10 newly constructed courthouses equipped with renewable energy systems, digitalised court records and broadband connectivity. He also urged lawyers to embrace technological advancements and prepare for emerging changes in legal practice. In his keynote address, former Vice President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, urged lawyers to move beyond litigation and legal interpretation to champion public interest, protect disadvantaged citizens and ensure that democracy delivers tangible benefits to the people. Osinbajo identified expensive legal services, prolonged court proceedings, judicial corruption and impunity as major obstacles to access to justice. item.title: 17 rescued, one injured as CNG commercial bus explodes on Lagos–Ibadan Expressway
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least ​17 people, including a driver, were rescued unhurt on Wednesday after a Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered commercial bus burst into flames following a gas explosion at Berger Bus Stop along the Lagos-bound section of the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway. ​One male passenger, who was seated at the rear of the fully loaded Hiace bus (registration number EKY 798 YK), sustained severe burn injuries and was rushed to the Lagos State Trauma and Emergency Centre at Toll Gate for urgent medical attention. ​According to eyewitnesses, the vehicle was conveying 18 occupants from the Mowe-Ibafo axis toward Lagos when it erupted into flames, triggering panic among passengers and motorists. Commenting on the accident, Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, through Director of Public Affairs and Enlightenment, Adebayo Taofiq, LASTMA personnel promptly mobilised to the scene to evacuate the occupants, while officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service extinguished the blaze to prevent it from spreading. Personnel from the Ojodu Police Division also provided security and maintained order throughout the rescue and firefighting operations. ​Commending the operation, Bakare-Oki praised the agency’s personnel for their swift intervention and thanked the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Nigeria Police Force for their collaboration. ​He noted that the incident underscores the importance of rapid emergency response and inter-agency synergy in mitigating road disasters. Bakare-Oki therefore urged commercial transport operators—particularly those running CNG-powered vehicles—to prioritise regular professional inspections, adhere to safety standards, and ensure the proper maintenance of their gas storage and delivery systems. item.title: Gov Yusuf presents N1.107trn 2027 budget, earmarks 63% for capital projects
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has presented a proposed budget of N1.107 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly. The budget, tagged “Budget of Consolidating Gains and Accelerated Rural Development,” is the fourth and final budget of the administration’s first tenure, which is expected to end on May 29, 2027. Presenting the estimates, Yusuf said the budget was designed to consolidate existing achievements, accelerate rural development and ensure the completion of ongoing projects before the expiration of his administration’s first term. The governor said his administration had achieved more than 90 per cent of the programmes, projects and policies outlined in its development blueprint. He, however, acknowledged that some commitments remained outstanding, adding that the 2027 budget would prioritise their completion, alongside strengthening essential public services. “This is not merely nominal. It is a fiscal commitment to ensure that no ongoing project is abandoned,” he said. He added that the budget would consolidate reforms in free education, primary healthcare revitalisation and urban renewal, while ensuring that residents benefit from government projects and programmes. Yusuf said the proposed budget would focus on education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, water supply and human capital development, which he described as central to improving productivity and living conditions in the state. Budget breakdown Giving a breakdown of the proposed expenditure, the governor said ₦693.47 billion was earmarked for capital expenditure, while ₦413.55 billion was allocated to recurrent expenditure. He said the proposed capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio was 63 per cent to 37 per cent, reflecting the administration’s intention to direct more resources towards infrastructure and other development projects while meeting its recurrent obligations. On revenue projections, Yusuf put the state’s total recurrent revenue at ₦692.64 billion, comprising ₦142.84 billion from internally generated revenue and revenue from the Federation Account. He said the projected recurrent revenue represented a 34 per cent decrease compared with the 2026 fiscal year. However, he projected a 73 per cent increase in internally generated revenue, attributing the growth to reforms at the Kano State Internal Revenue Service, including digital revenue administration and the expansion of the Easy Tax digitisation initiative. The governor further said the state expected ₦354.38 billion in capital receipts from grants and loans, alongside an opening balance of ₦60 billion to finance the proposed budget. He said the allocations would support projects and programmes across the state’s economic and social sectors. Yusuf added that the government would prioritise completing ongoing projects and strengthening existing programmes before the end of its first tenure in May 2027. item.title: Man Utd ‘reach verbal agreement’ with Pochettino to replace Carrick
item.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. – Turbulent reign – Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. Carrick has presided over United’s slide to 18th place — their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th. He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss. item.title: Prison Break actor Stacy Keach dies at 85
item.description: American actor Stacy Keach, renowned for his roles in television and film productions spanning more than six decades, has died at the age of 85. Keach died on Tuesday at his home in Magdalenka, Poland, following a prolonged battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi Keach, announced his death in a statement, describing him as a courageous fighter whose resilience defined both his personal life and acting career. “It is with profound sadness and a broken heart that I announce the passing of my darling husband, Stacy Keach. After a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, Stacy peacefully departed this world,” she said. She described the late actor as a legendary performer whose work earned him admiration from audiences worldwide, adding that his death had left an immeasurable void in the family. Keach began his acting career on Broadway in the 1960s before transitioning to film in the 1970s. He gained recognition for his performance alongside Faye Dunaway in the 1971 film Doc. He became particularly popular for portraying private investigator Mike Hammer in several television productions, including Mickey Spillane’s Mike Hammer and The New Mike Hammer. His other notable screen appearances included the television series Prison Break, Blue Bloods and Titus, as well as films such as The Long Riders, Nebraska and The Bourne Legacy. The actor also appeared in the biblical miniseries Jesus of Nazareth, where he portrayed Barabbas. Over a career spanning approximately 60 years, Keach accumulated more than 200 film and television credits and earned recognition as an accomplished interpreter of Shakespeare. His career also included stage performances and a Tony Award nomination, further establishing his reputation as a versatile actor. Keach came from a family with strong ties to the entertainment industry. His father, Stacy Keach Sr., was a respected actor, while his brother, James Keach, is also an actor and filmmaker. He was previously reported to have suffered a heart attack on stage in Chicago in 2017. Keach is survived by his wife, Małgosia, their children, Karolina and Shannon, grandchildren and other members of the extended family. In her tribute, his wife said his unforgettable voice, remarkable spirit and love for his family would remain with them forever. item.title: Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel
item.description: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for the shirt-pull on Alexander Isak in their Premier League match against Arsenal, an expert panel ruled Wednesday. The Sweden striker’s shirt was tugged by Gunners defender Jurrien Timber in the match at Anfield on November 1, which Premier League champions Arsenal won 1-0. Referee Andy Madley let the incident pass without sanction, and video assistant referee Stuart Attwell decided against recommending a review. The decision was criticised at the time by pundits such as Jamie Carragher and Ian Wright, and now the five-person Key Match Incidents panel has said a penalty should have been awarded. Madley’s decision was criticised by four of the panellists, who felt Timber’s challenge met the threshold for a holding offence, while three felt Attwell should have intervened because it was a clear and obvious error by Madley. Isak did not make any protest about Timber’s shirt-pull to the on-field officials, in a match which was settled by Kai Havertz’s goal for the Gunners. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola, asked after the match whether Isak should have gone down following the challenge, replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them (the players), go down, because they (the officials) are not going to call it otherwise. “And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down. “But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.” The post Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Throwback: 10 songs that have defined Nigeria’s Detty December
item.description: Before the December concert rush, packed nightclubs, beach parties and returning diaspora crowds became synonymous with Detty December, Nigerian music had already established the festive season as its biggest playground. Every December, a new collection of songs takes over the streets, clubs, weddings, concerts and parties, providing the soundtrack to the celebrations as Nigerians round off the year. From Wizkid’s infectious melodies and Naira Marley’s street anthems to Portable’s Zazoo Zeh and Seyi Vibez’s Chance, some records have become inseparable from memories of particular festive seasons. READ MORE: Although Nigerians have celebrated Christmas and New Year with music and parties for decades, the phrase Detty December gained popularity around 2016, with singer Mr Eazi credited with popularising it through his concert promotion. Over the years, the culture has grown into a major entertainment season, with Lagos becoming a destination for returning Nigerians, international visitors and music lovers. As another festive season approaches, here is a throwback to 10 songs that have defined Nigeria’s Detty December experience over the years. 1. 2016 – Mad Over You by Runtown Few songs captured the mood of the 2016 festive season quite like Runtown’s ‘Mad Over You’. Released towards the end of the year, the song became a massive hit, with its Ghana-inspired Pon Pon sound, catchy melody and romantic lyrics making it a favourite across clubs, parties and radio stations. The record arrived at a time when Nigerian music was embracing a more melodic, highlife-influenced sound, moving away from some of the faster dance-driven records that had dominated previous years. Its popularity extended beyond Nigeria, becoming a major hit across West Africa and one of the songs many music lovers associate with the early Detty December era. 2. 2017 – Manya by Mut4y featuring Wizkid Wizkid returned to the festive-season conversation in 2017 with ‘Manya’, a collaboration with producer Mut4y. Built around an infectious rhythm and an interpolation of the popular Ghanaian song ‘Akohoma Womu’, the track quickly became a party favourite. Released during a year in which Wizkid enjoyed significant international recognition with his ‘Sounds From the Other Side’ project, ‘Manya’ helped maintain his dominance on the Nigerian music scene. From clubs to concerts and street parties, the song became one of the defining sounds of the 2017 festive season, competing with Kizz Daniel’s ‘Yeba’ and Reekado Banks’ ‘Like’. 3. 2018 – Able God by Chinko Ekun featuring Lil Kesh and Zlatan If there was one street anthem that Nigerians could hardly escape during the 2018 festive season, it was ‘Able God’. Chinko Ekun recruited Lil Kesh and Zlatan for the Rexxie-produced record, which became popular for its energetic delivery, memorable hook and danceable production. item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity – UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has disclosed. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the growing influx was creating a deepening humanitarian and protection crisis in Niger, which is already hosting more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to UNHCR, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of worsening insecurity in northern Nigeria. The agency’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. In October alone, about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua. UNHCR disclosed that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. The agency expressed concern over the difficult conditions facing the displaced families, many of whom are living in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. It said some women were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported increasing cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The refugee agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, revealing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. The absence of proper documentation, it warned, was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The situation is further complicated by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in the Diffa region, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing humanitarian pressure, UNHCR acknowledged the support provided by Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the allocation of land for temporary shelters. The agency, however, appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for immediate critical interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without essential humanitarian assistance. item.title: Mbappe misses France training ahead of Italy clash
item.description: France captain Kylian Mbappe did not take part in team training on Wednesday and remained “under treatment” ahead of his country’s Nations League match against Italy, Les Bleus’ coaching staff said. The French coaching staff did not provide any further details regarding the 27-year-old’s physical condition. The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury. Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zinedine Zidane’s first match as coach against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee. After three wins and a draw in four matches, France top Group A1 of the Nations League and are well on course to qualify for the quarter-finals ahead of their final two pool-stage fixtures against Italy on Thursday in Milan, and Turkey on Sunday in Bordeaux. item.title: Xenophobic attacks: Help South Africans, don’t punish them — OAU don
item.description: …As varsity’s International Relations Department marks 50th anniversary By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Federal Government has been urged to adopt a sympathetic approach towards South Africa over the recent xenophobic attacks, rather than resort to punitive measures, with a don at the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, saying South Africans need help at a difficult time. A Professor of International Relations at OAU, Charles Ukeje, said the xenophobic violence was regrettable, particularly given Nigeria’s significant contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Ukeje spoke during a press conference organised to herald the 50th anniversary of the university’s Department of International Relations at the campus. He blamed the attacks partly on the failure of successive South African governments to adequately educate their citizens about the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. According to him, proper education about the contributions of other African nations could have helped foster a stronger sense of brotherhood among South Africans and other Africans. He said: “I believe that the xenophobic violence in South Africa is very regrettable. It is regrettable because this is a country which the rest of the continent, particularly Nigeria, helped to midwife in the context of apartheid. “So, in the post-apartheid era, you would expect that the South Africans will be more and better disposed to the rest of Africans, given the amount of sacrifice that Nigerians and other African countries have made in the bid to end apartheid in that country. “It is regrettable that generations of South African leaders, upon achieving an end to apartheid, really did not adequately educate their citizens on the role the whole of Africa played. “Perhaps, if they had done that, things would have been different. Perhaps, the ordinary South African citizens on the street would treat and see other Africans as brothers.” On Nigeria’s response, the don said the country should maintain its longstanding commitment to Africa as the centrepiece of its foreign policy. He urged the Federal Government to demonstrate leadership by showing understanding towards South Africa, despite the hostility some of its citizens might harbour towards Nigerians. “In terms of how Nigeria should respond, Africa has always been the centrepiece of Nigeria’s foreign policy. I don’t think that is going to change. “I think Nigeria has the responsibility to continue to see itself as a leader on the continent. I think that role for Nigeria is perhaps more important today than it was anytime. “And I’m looking forward to the Nigerian government not really wielding the big stick against South Africa, but to actually acknowledge that the country and its citizens are facing very difficult circumstances at this time and we need to be more sympathetic to them, even with the amount of disdain that the ordinary ci

item.title: Lagos govt warns PSPs over refuse crisis, demands results
item.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. The government said it had fulfilled its responsibility by rehabilitating the facilities and their access roads, leaving waste operators with no further excuses for the persistent refuse crisis across the state. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the previously closed Solus dumpsite in Alimosho Local Government Area. Wahab said the government expected PSP operators to improve waste collection and evacuation across their areas of operation, stressing that residents deserved value for the services they paid for. “Too much is given, so much more is expected. There are no more excuses,” the commissioner said, recounting his message to the leadership of the PSP operators. “The state government has done its own bit; let your PSP members also put their skin in it and see how they can achieve what we set out jointly to achieve because they suggested we put this into play and now we’ve done it for them.” According to him, the decision to reopen Solus followed proposals by waste operators to rehabilitate the facility rather than wait for the development of new dumpsites around Badagry and Epe. He explained that Solus, located within Lagos West, serves several local government areas, including Alimosho, Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Mushin, Badagry, Ikeja, Ojo and Apapa. The commissioner said the contractor handling the rehabilitation had assured the government that the repaired access road would last at least one year, subject to quarterly maintenance. He added that the facility was expected to accommodate at least 100 trucks daily, significantly improving waste evacuation in the affected areas. “100 trucks from this axis coming here to discharge gives us the comfort that our streets, our homes will not be littered with waste,” Wahab said. Addressing complaints by residents over the failure of some PSP operators to collect refuse regularly, the commissioner said the state government would enforce its polluter-pays policy to ensure operators delivered the services for which residents paid. He warned that the government would take necessary measures to hold defaulting operators accountable. LAWMA restructuring Wahab also confirmed a major restructuring of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), ordered by the state governor, as part of efforts to improve waste management operations. He announced the appointment of Juwon Akinyemi as Acting Managing Director, Dr Tjani Olorunwa as Acting Executive Director of Operations, and Kunle Adebiyi as substantive Executive Director of Finance. item.title: ADC protesters take Mark judgment dispute to NJC, UN, EU, UK, US embassies
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) on Wednesday staged a protest at the Federal High Court in Abuja, demanding the release of the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment nullifying the party’s National Working Committee led by former Senate President, David Mark. The protesters accused the trial judge, Justice Peter Lifu, of withholding the November 5 judgment despite an application by the party’s lawyers and payment of the prescribed fees, arguing that the delay was frustrating their efforts to challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal. The protesters also extended their campaign beyond the court premises, storming the headquarters of the United Nations (UN), as well as the European Union (EU), United Kingdom and United States embassies in Abuja, where they submitted letters seeking diplomatic attention and support for what they described as due process, the right of appeal and credible elections in Nigeria. The letters bore the subject: “Urgent Appeal for Diplomatic Attention and Support for Due Process, the Right of Appeal and Credible Elections in Nigeria – Re: Judgment Delivered on 5th November, 2026 in Suit No: FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025 (Nafiu Bala Gombe Vs. ADC & Ors).” Speaking during the protest, a former Acting Chairman of the ADC in the Federal Capital Territory, Yusuf Shehu Tijani, described the judgment as a sham and called on the National Judicial Council (NJC) to intervene. “Our reason for coming here today is what Justice Lifu is doing. He is holding on to the sham judgment he said he passed. He should send the CTC, so that we can get it and appeal the judgment. “Moreover, the Supreme Court already affirmed the leadership of Senator David Mark as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress. So why is the High Court going against that recognition, saying he’s passing a judgment? “Now the judgment you passed, give us the Certified True Copy so that we can appeal. He is refusing to do that. That is why we are here,” Tijani said. He said the protest was intended to draw the NJC’s attention to the alleged delay and compel the judge to release the document. “So the protest is to call on the NJC to pressure this man, let him do what is right, because justice must prevail in Nigeria. This is not a jungle. This is a country that has laws, that has rules, and we have to follow the Constitution of the country. “The stated law is that he should send the CTC so that we can appeal the judgment, which is a sham judgment in the first place,” he added. The protest followed a November 10 petition addressed to the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, by members of the ADC candidates’ forum, demanding the immediate release of the judgment. item.title: Police probe Blord over armed officers’ escort
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord, at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the deployment of the officers as “unlawful and illegal”, saying an investigation had commenced into the incident. Iniedu disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday while reacting to the video. “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity,” he wrote. The video, which Blord shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, showed him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, accompanied by armed police officers dressed in camouflage uniforms and tactical gear. The businessman was seen wearing a red-and-white striped traditional cap associated with the Kwankwaso political brand. He was also seen arriving in a black Cadillac with the personalised number plate, “B-LORD”. Other scenes in the footage showed Blord walking alongside the armed officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appeared to be his business premises. The officers were seen providing him with an escort and opening the vehicle door for him. Captioning the video, Blord wrote: “Back to base, business as usual. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another Instagram post, the businessman said he had been in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons (VIPs) across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu gave the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would henceforth be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the measure was aimed at strengthening police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised deployment of police escorts. item.title: Govt Scared of Peter Obi’s Popularity, Campaign Camp Pushes Back Over Flamingos Airport Encounter
item.description: Representatives of Peter Obi have dismissed accusations that the presidential candidate was “playing to the gallery” during a recent encounter with Nigeria’s national U-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, at the airport. Addressing criticism from political opponents and government commentators, a representative for Obi’s camp said the incident was a spontaneous moment during routine domestic travel, claiming federal officials and the ruling party are unsettled by the opposition leader’s widespread public support. ‘A Man on the Move’ Rebutting claims that the airport greeting was a staged publicity stunt, Obi’s campaign team clarified that the candidate was at the airport to board a commercial flight for scheduled engagements across the country when he crossed paths with the victorious sports delegation. “I don’t understand what they mean by our candidate playing to the gallery,” the spokesperson said. “Every Nigerian knows that Peter Obi is a man on the move. He has engagements across the country, and at that time, he was at the airport just like any other traveller trying to catch a flight to his next destination.” The statement emphasised that meeting the Flamingos—who were returning from international competition—was entirely coincidental, adding that Obi’s decision to approach the team was an act of national pride. “It just so happened that the Flamingos were there at the same time, and like any patriotic Nigerian, he simply wanted to greet them and congratulate them on their victory.” Pattern of Restrictions The campaign further alleged that this was not an isolated event, asserting that security or administrative barriers have previously been used to prevent Obi from interacting with victorious Nigerian athletes during public appearances. Obi’s camp described the government’s reaction as indicative of political anxiety over his public visibility. “This is not the first time this has happened,” the representative noted. “He has been prevented from greeting victorious Nigerian athletes before. This latest incident just shows how jittery the government is. They do not want him taking the spotlight because wherever Peter Obi goes, Nigerians rally behind him.” ﻿ ﻿ Political Friction Ahead of Elections The clash underscores the heightened sensitivity surrounding public engagements and political optics as major parties structure their national campaigns. While government supporters have accused opposition figures of leveraging national sports achievements for political leverage, Obi’s campaign maintained that public enthusiasm during his travel movements remains organic and unscripted. “While it is understandable that they are scared, it is pathetic, to say the least,” the spokesperson concluded, reiterating that the presidential candidate will continue his scheduled nationwide tours and citizen engagements despite ongoing political scrutiny. item.title: Troops ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​⁠‍‍‌​‌‌​apprehend father, son for alleged terrorism in Sokoto forest
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have apprehended two suspected terrorists (father and son) in Sokoto State. The suspects, identified as Muhammadu Ali and his son, Umaru Ali, were arrested at Bauni Forest in Tangaza Local Government Area. The operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday said the operation was conducted by troops of 248 Battalion, supported by the French Special Forces and the NCTC-Office of the National Security Adviser tactical team. The report said the suspects were apprehended at about 10:00 a.m. on Wednesday and were believed to be from the Bauni village area. According to the report, items recovered during the operation included one AK-47 rifle, one magazine containing three rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, ₦9,760 and three motorcycle tubes. The report said the suspects were in the custody of 8 Military Intelligence Battalions for further investigation. item.title: Many terrorists neutralised as military sustains pressure on enclaves
item.description: Scores of terrorists have been neutralised across different communities in the Northern region of the country following the pressure sustained in their enclaves by the troops of the Nigerian military. The troops, in different operations sustained pressure on the criminals and dismantled criminal networks with a view to protecting lives and property, and restoring lasting peace and security across the country. Daily Trust reports that the development was in line with the commitment of the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the leadership of General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede. The four-star general, has at different fora maintained that he would continue to ensure that all law-abiding Nigerians, particularly those in the Northern Nigeria sleep with their two eyes closed. Updating Nigerians on the efforts being made to restore peace across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja disclosed that consistent efforts were made to deny terrorists, kidnappers, gunrunners and other criminal groups’ freedom of action between October 30th and November 5th, 2026. Terrorists suffer heavy losses in Northeast Checks showed that in the North East geopolitical zone, troops of Operation HADIN KAI inflicted heavy losses on terrorists who attempted to strike at troops’ locations in Borno and Yobe States. Subsequently, troops pressed home the advantage with clearance operations and a wave of arrests. On the night of October 29th, 2026, terrorists approached Buni Yadi in Gujba LGA of Yobe State, from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. However, troops countered the attack and subsequent exploitation on 30 October 30th, 2026 discovered the bodies of 48 terrorists, along with 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, a 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. The following day, troops’ operations around Apama and Jauro Bashir along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three corpses, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The senior military officer confirmed that on the same day, terrorists also attempted to infiltrate a troops’ location at Bitta in Gwoza LGA of Borno State but were forced to retreat. He added, “Exploitation at first light recovered the bodies of seven terrorists, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. “Troops also received several surrendered members of terrorist groups, rescued escapees and dismantled terrorist support networks across the theatre. “Between 2 – 4 November 2026, twelve terrorist fighters and family members surrendered at New Abaram Resettlement Village and Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA in Borno State.” On November 2nd, 2026, troops rescued a female abductee who had escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road.
